boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments at Northeastern’s Boston campus, including reservable rooms, silent spaces, and collaboration areas.

cards.title: Snell Library Open Study Space
cards.subtitle: Snell Library • 376 Huntington Avenue
cards.notes: Choose from the library’s soft seating, chairs, tables, and booths; use the setting that fits an individual reading block or a working session.
cards.short_summary: Flexible seating across Snell Library’s open study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Snell Library provides open study space with soft seating, chairs, tables, and booths.
cards.access_notes: Located in Snell Library; follow the library’s current visitor-access policy and code of conduct.

cards.title: Room 255 Quiet Study Space
cards.subtitle: Second floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Head to Room 255 when it is not occupied by library staff and set up for a designated quiet-study session away from phone calls.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study room on Snell’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 255 is designated as quiet study space whenever it is not occupied by library staff.
cards.access_notes: Use only when the room is not occupied by library staff.

cards.title: Graduate Study Room 320
cards.subtitle: Third floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this silent open-study room for focused reading or writing; keep the glass-enclosed area quiet for everyone working there.
cards.short_summary: Silent open study space reserved for graduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 320 is a silent open study space available for graduate students.
cards.access_notes: Available to graduate students; observe Snell Library’s current access and conduct rules.

cards.title: Graduate Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Inside Room 320 • Third floor, Snell Library
cards.notes: Graduate and doctoral students can reserve a group room inside the glass-enclosed graduate study space when a project needs a shared workspace.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group rooms within Snell’s graduate study area.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduate group study rooms on Snell’s third floor are reservable for graduate and doctoral students and are located inside Room 320.
cards.access_notes: For graduate and doctoral students; reserve during service-desk hours under the library’s booking policies.

cards.title: Silent Study Room 490
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor • Snell Library
cards.notes: Use Room 490 for silent open study, especially for tasks that benefit from a no-conversation setting such as close reading or drafting.
cards.short_summary: A silent fourth-floor study room open to everyone.
cards.evidence_claim: Room 490 is a silent open study space available to everyone.
cards.access_notes: Available to everyone, subject to Snell Library’s current access and conduct rules.

cards.title: Silent Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Inside Room 490 • Fourth floor, Snell Library
cards.notes: Reserve a silent individual room inside Room 490 for a private focused block, then arrive on time so the reservation remains active.
cards.short_summary: Reservable individual rooms in Snell’s silent-study area.
cards.evidence_claim: Silent individual study rooms are located inside Room 490 and are available for reservation during service-desk hours.
cards.access_notes: Reserve during service-desk hours; library reservations may be made up to one week ahead and are limited to three hours at a time.

cards.title: Snell Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lower level, first, second, and fourth floors
cards.notes: Reserve a group study room before meeting classmates; select a room on the lower level, first, second, or fourth floor that suits the group’s route.
cards.short_summary: Student-reservable group rooms on four Snell floors.
cards.evidence_claim: All students can reserve Snell Library group study rooms on the lower level and the first, second, and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: Reserve during service-desk hours; reservations can be made up to one week in advance, for up to three hours at a time.

cards.title: Snell Library Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Second and fourth floors
cards.notes: Book an individual room on Snell’s second or fourth floor when you need a reservable personal workspace rather than an open seating area.
cards.short_summary: Reservable individual rooms on Snell’s upper floors.
cards.evidence_claim: All students can reserve individual study rooms on Snell Library’s second and fourth floors.
cards.access_notes: Reserve during service-desk hours; each student may make no more than three room reservations per week.

cards.entity_name: Centers for Digital Scholarship Presentation Space
cards.title: CDS Presentation Space
cards.subtitle: Snell Library • Boston campus
cards.notes: Use this designated presentation setting when preparing collaborative digital-scholarship work that benefits from a shared display and hybrid-capable space.
cards.short_summary: A presentation environment within the Centers for Digital Scholarship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Centers for Digital Scholarship in Snell Library includes a presentation space and Teams-enabled collaborative spaces.
cards.access_notes: Consult the Centers for Digital Scholarship’s booking information and space-usage policies before planning a session.

cards.entity_name: Centers for Digital Scholarship Large Collaboration Space
cards.title: CDS Large Collaboration Space
cards.subtitle: Snell Library • Boston campus
cards.notes: Plan a collaborative work session in this CDS setting when a team needs project, lab, meeting, or hybrid communication infrastructure in one place.
cards.short_summary: A large group-work setting in Snell’s digital scholarship center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Centers for Digital Scholarship includes large collaboration spaces as part of its project, lab, meeting, presentation, and collaborative areas.
cards.access_notes: Consult the Centers for Digital Scholarship’s booking information and space-usage policies before planning a session.
